text:
GENERATE BURST GS-SPA -- Run C-9 Phase 2 (Matt R-C9-105 / R-C9-98): the PAINTED TEXTURE of the fire sorceress's battle-mage armour, sheet 1 of 2. task_id "GS-SPA".

IMAGE 1 is a sheet of TEN renders of ONE 3D model of a woman standing in an A-pose, seen from a little above (19.77 degrees), on flat pure #00ff00. Top row, left to right: facing the lower right (south-east); facing the lower left (south-west); facing the viewer's RIGHT in profile (east); facing the viewer's LEFT in profile (west); facing away to the upper left (north-west); facing away to the upper right (north-east); FACING THE VIEWER (south). Bottom row, left to right: seen from BEHIND (north); a CLOSE-UP of her head from the lower right, three-quarter; a CLOSE-UP of her HEAD from the front. They are renders of the model: every OUTLINE, POSE, POSITION and SIZE is correct and must not change; the surface colour is the 3D model's own flat, muddy texture.
IMAGE 2 is her APPROVED battle-mage sheet: a lean, athletic woman with light, weathered skin and dark hair in one thick rear braid, in a SCARLET wool hood with a narrow gold-rune border falling to a short shoulder cape; under it a fine steel mail coif and a slim steel diadem with an orange ember gem; a POLISHED STEEL breastplate with EMBER-RED etched runes down its centre, with steel spaulders; mail sleeves and a mail skirt over a quilted CHARCOAL arming gown; steel gauntlets and vambraces; a SCARLET tabard with a gold-rune border and a scarlet sash; dark leggings with steel cuisses, knee cops and greaves; brown boots. IMAGE 3 is a STYLE reference ONLY: copy its HAND (the warm dark-brown ink line that varies in weight, transparent watercolour washes that pool and granulate, fine hatching in the shadows, cream paper highlights); copy nothing else from it.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and deliver ONE 1536x1024 sheet in which EVERY figure is repainted as the woman of IMAGE 2 seen from that direction, in IMAGE 3's hand, inside exactly that view's outline, position and size.
THIS PAINTING BECOMES THE MODEL'S TEXTURE: it is projected back onto the 3D model from these ten cameras and blended. So:
1. ONE woman in ten views, not ten women: the same colours and the same details in every view. Any disagreement becomes a seam.
2. Paint the SURFACE, not the lighting: soft even light; no cast shadows, no dark side, no rim light. Tone comes from her own colours and the pen hatching.
3. Stay inside the outlines: do not paint beyond a silhouette or change any outline, pose, hand or foot.
THE COLOURS MUST STAY APART at a small size -- the reason for this painting: STEEL is cool silver-grey with blue-grey shadows and crisp ink edges, NOT flat pale grey; MAIL is a darker steel texture of fine rings; the hood, cape, tabard and sash are SCARLET with GOLD borders; the gown is CHARCOAL; her face is light warm skin; her hair dark.
THE SASH knot sits on her LEFT hip. ADD NOTHING IMAGE 2 does not show: no weapon, no staff, no book.
THE TWO HEAD CLOSE-UPS are her identity: the same face as IMAGE 2, larger. More detail is welcome; a different face is not.

BACKGROUND: keep it flat pure #00ff00. If the image model returns a darker or gradient background anyway, still deliver the image: the figures are cut out by their exact 3D outlines.

Two image_gen EDIT calls: variants a and b. ONE retry per variant only if a view's outline, pose, facing or position changed, a view is missing, the woman differs between views, the colours merged into one tan, a piece is on the wrong arm, or a head close-up is a different face -- name the reason. Never retry for the background colour. Copy outputs to out/GS-SPA_a.png and out/GS-SPA_b.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "GS-SPA"; images = the files with prompt, references (role + path) and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.

IMAGE 2 -- her approved battle-mage sheet (GS-SHOOD, Matt's pick): the look
IMAGE 3 -- STYLE reference ONLY (Matt-supplied, R-C9-69): the hand
